about: The corrections this site has asked other publishers to make, kept by liaison@php.newsroom (brief: admin/content/briefs/2026-10-22__brief__the-corrections-liaison.md; desk: admin/liaison/README.md). Every request starts from a fact-check finding or contradiction in data/factcheck.json, quotes the publisher only from a capture in the evidence vault, and is on this site before any message is sent. Nothing here has been sent: sending waits for the editor and a security change to who the mail agent may write to.

statuses.means: Written from a fact-check record; not yet read by the editor
Waits on something named in blocked_by: usually an open finding against this site's own wording on the same point
The editor has read it and said it may go; not sent
The mail agent sent it to the publisher's corrections channel; the log has the time
The publisher replied without a change yet
The publisher changed the text; a new capture shows it
The publisher answered and kept the text; their reason is recorded
Fourteen days after sending, no answer; nothing more is sent

requests.point: The headline says the flaws affect 70% of the Internet; the post's own body says PHP powers 70% of all websites.

said.words: PHP2Shell: AI uncovers critical RCE vulnerabilities affecting 70% of the Internet
a popular general-purpose scripting language that powers 70% of all websites in the world.
a decade-old PHP Core vulnerability reaching CVSS 9.2 severity impacting 70% of the Internet.

requests.evidence: The 70% is the usual web-technology survey figure: the share of websites whose server-side language is known that use PHP (Cloudflare links it to W3Techs; Tenable and Imperva name W3Techs, at 69.3% and over 69%). It is a share of websites, not of hosts, traffic or the Internet, and it counts sites that use PHP at all, not installations running an affected version. Every outlet in our evidence vault that carries the figure traces back to this post.
requests.suggested: PHP2Shell: AI uncovers critical RCE vulnerabilities in PHP, the language behind about 70% of websites whose server-side language is known

channel.note: Wiz's published press or research contact, from its own site; captured before use

requests.point: The live page puts "roughly 70%" in quotation marks as Wiz's estimate; Wiz's own words have no "roughly", and the 70% is a share of websites using PHP, not a measure of how much of the internet is affected.

said.words: with cyber-security firm Wiz estimating that "roughly 70%" of the internet is affected, though the BBC is unable to independently verify that figure.

requests.evidence: The words in quotation marks are not in either capture of Wiz's own words: the blog headline and the X post say '70% of the Internet', the blog body says '70% of all websites in the world'. The figure itself is a survey's share of websites whose server-side language is known that use PHP, not a share of the internet affected. The BBC's own caveat, that it could not verify the figure, is right and is kept in the suggestion.
requests.suggested: with cyber-security firm Wiz saying the flaws affect "70% of the Internet", a figure that matches surveys of how many websites use PHP rather than a count of vulnerable systems, and that the BBC has been unable to independently verify.
